statement: Legacy adapters only describe foreign evidence; they never make foreign container structures authoritative EAM state.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/legacy-observation-model-v1.md L17-18 (adapter never constructs special-case EAM entries)
evidence_in_source: module doc comment; enforced structurally by adapters projecting through plan_observed_archive

statement: The legacy module publicly exposes submodules export, import, lom, migration, sevenz, stream, tar, zip and re-exports the LOM types (ConflictClass, LegacyArchiveObservation, LegacyAuthority, LegacyConflict, entry/field observations, evidence location, observed value, resolution, ObservationValidity).
LegacyAuthority identifies one independently observed foreign authority by format string, structure string and u64 instance; authority names are free-form strings chosen per adapter.
decision_needed: Should authority format/structure names be a frozen registry rather than adapter-local strings?

statement: LegacyEvidenceLocation is an (offset,length) u64 pair with no explicit layer identifier; the byte space is implied only by the observation's authority (outer transport vs decoded child).
research_needed: Check that consumers can unambiguously map evidence to layer byte spaces for multi-layer sources.

statement: ObservationValidity has three parser states: Valid, Invalid, Uninterpreted.

LegacyObservedValue is type-erased as Bytes, Unsigned, Signed, Text or Boolean; display_compact renders Bytes only as '<n> bytes', so byte-valued conflicts lose their exact values when summarized into provenance resolutions.
decision_needed: Should ConversionResolution observed_values keep exact bytes (e.g., hex) instead of compact length summaries?

statement: LegacyFieldObservation<T> carries semantic_field name, authority, exact raw_value bytes, optional interpreted value, evidence location and validity.
LegacyEntryObservation groups all field observations for one foreign entry ordinal.
Exactly four conflict classes are frozen with stable strings: omission, refinement, divergence, irreconcilable; unit test conflict_classes_are_stable (lom.rs:149-155) pins the strings.

LegacyResolution is a free-text action string plus optional selected authority; LegacyConflict records semantic field, all authorities, observed values, evidence, class and optional resolution. Resolution actions are prose, not typed stable codes.
decision_needed: Should resolution actions become typed, versioned identifiers so provenance is machine-comparable across adapter versions?

statement: LegacyArchiveObservation holds source_format, SHA-256 source_digest, archive-level fields, entries and conflicts; observation_count saturates the sum of archive and entry fields; conflict_count filters by class.
LegacySourceFormat has eleven variants with ids zip, 7z, tar, gzip, zstd, xz, bzip2, tar.gz, tar.zst, tar.xz, tar.bz2; the four tar.* variants map to a transport and require a tar child.

Only the eleven exact format tokens parse; aliases (tgz, tbz2, txz) and all other formats (OCI, NAR, RAR5, cpio, ar, WIM, squashfs, ISO, lzip, LZ4 frame, lzma-alone, .Z, brotli) are rejected as Unsupported EB_LEGACY_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED.
research_needed: Adoption/corpus study to rank which additional adapters matter for v1.
decision_needed: Which additional legacy adapters (OCI layers, cpio, ar/.deb, RAR5, WIM, squashfs, lzip, LZ4) are in scope for v1?

statement: LegacyImportPolicy groups the ZIP, 7z, tar and wrapper policies without merging format-specific rules; Default uses each sub-policy default.

LegacyConversionReport exposes the LOM, synthesized ancestors, layer list, wrapper member count, decoded child digest, projection ('archive' or 'single-file:<name>') and format statistics; LegacyImportResult pairs it with the Archive.

Format detection order: ZIP signature at offset 0 (local, EOCD, spanning marker), then 7z signature, then gzip/zstd/xz/bzip2 magic, then tar checksum preflight, then any ZIP EOCD signature within the last 65,557 bytes.

Transport magic sniffing (e.g., bzip2 'BZh'+digit, 2-byte gzip magic) runs before tar checksum validation, and explicit --from must match detection, so a valid tar whose first member name begins with such magic is detected as a transport and becomes unimportable.
research_needed: Construct fixtures (tar whose first name starts 'BZh9') and measure misdetection; survey detection false-positive rates on a corpus.
decision_needed: Should a structurally valid explicit --from (full tar checksum) override weak magic sniffing?

statement: Any otherwise unrecognized input containing a ZIP EOCD signature in its last 65,557 bytes is classified as ZIP (covers prepended/SFX data); acceptance is delegated to the ZIP adapter.
research_needed: Measure false positives for binary files containing PK\x05\x06 near the end.

statement: import_strict refuses unrecognized sources with Unsupported EB_LEGACY_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED; when no explicit format is given the detected format is used.

Byte/structure detection is authoritative: an explicit zip, 7z or tar format must equal the detected format or import fails Nonconforming EB_LEGACY_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED (format_mismatch, import.rs:425-435); test explicit_format_must_match_actual_framing (import.rs:587-602).
--entry-name is valid only for standalone compressed streams; supplying it for ZIP, 7z or tar sources is PolicyRefused EB_CLI_USAGE (also import.rs:190-194, 224-228).
ZIP strict results are mapped with layers ['zip'], projection 'archive', zero wrapper members and no format statistics.
7z strict results report format statistics folders, solid-folders, coders and encoded-header (0/1) in the conversion report.

For wrapper formats the transport is verified and decoded first; if the decoded child is structurally tar it is always sent to the single tar observer/resolver, and --entry-name cannot override a valid decoded tar.
Test shows tar.gz/tar.zst/tar.xz/tar.bz2 imports yield the same LAI and PCR as the bare tar but a different AUX (provenance), and INDEXED vs STREAM encodings share LAI/PCR/AUX while PCI differs.
When tar.gz/tar.zst/tar.xz/tar.bz2 is explicitly requested but the decoded child is not structurally tar, import fails Nonconforming EB_TAR_STRUCTURE_INVALID.

Only one transport layer is composed: a decoded child is either tar or one opaque file. Nested transports (gzip of xz, tar.gz inside tar), and importing a .tar.gz as a single opaque file, are not supported.
decision_needed: Should nested transports or an explicit opaque single-file projection of a tar child be allowed?

statement: looks_like_tar accepts any child of >=1024 bytes, 512-multiple, starting with two zero blocks, so a compressed all-zero payload (e.g., zeroed image) imports as an empty tar archive and --entry-name is refused.
research_needed: Fixture test: gzip of 1 MiB zeros with and without --entry-name.
decision_needed: Should standalone vs tar projection require explicit caller choice when the child is all zeros?

statement: A standalone (non-tar) compressed stream requires an explicit --entry-name; otherwise PolicyRefused EB_CLI_USAGE. Covered by test standalone_stream_requires_and_validates_an_explicit_entry_name (import.rs:548-585).

Standalone projection creates synthesized ancestor directories with empty metadata and one File entry whose only metadata is core.executable=false; wrapper FNAME, MTIME and other header fields never become path or metadata.
Standalone provenance records one Omission resolution per synthesized ancestor and one Refinement 'layer.transport-decoded-child' binding outer source digest and decoded digest with member count.
Standalone adapter id is '<format>-stream-strict/v1' (e.g., gzip-stream-strict/v1), import_mode 'strict', source_entry_count 1, unsupported metadata '<format>.wrapper-metadata', outcome 'success'.
Standalone FidelityReport captures only legacy.conversion-provenance, lists '<format>.wrapper-metadata' as unavailable, and sets platform 'legacy:<format>'.

Standalone entry names are refused if empty, starting with '/' or '\', containing any backslash or NUL, having ':' at byte 1, or containing empty, '.' or '..' components; refusals reuse EB_TAR_UNSAFE_PATH even for non-tar transports.
decision_needed: Should standalone-stream name refusals get a transport-neutral reason code instead of EB_TAR_UNSAFE_PATH?

statement: Import-side path checks (standalone and tar, tar.rs:1352-1376) and LogicalPath allow colons beyond byte 1, control characters, newlines, trailing dots/spaces and Windows device names, while ZIP/tar export refuses several of these, so imported archives may be unexportable.
research_needed: Cross-platform extraction matrix for names with ':', control chars, newlines, device names.
decision_needed: Should strict import refuse or flag names that no frozen export profile or common platform can materialize?

statement: Transport metadata is auxiliary foreign evidence and is never promoted to an Entry name or metadata field.
Transport magic constants: gzip 1F 8B; Zstandard frame 0xFD2FB528; skippable frames 0x184D2A50-0x184D2A5F; XZ FD '7zXZ' 00; bzip2 is 'BZh' followed by '1'-'9' (stream.rs:92).
TransportFormat has four variants with ids gzip, zstd, xz, bzip2.
No transport adapters exist for LZ4 frame, lzip, lzma-alone, zlib, Unix compress (.Z) or brotli; detect returns None for them.
decision_needed: Are LZ4 frame and lzip transports required for v1 (adapter priority)?

statement: WrapperImportPolicy defaults: max_source_bytes 4 GiB, max_members 1,000,000, max_metadata_bytes 64 MiB, max_decoded_child_bytes 16 GiB, max_aggregate_decoded_bytes 16 GiB, max_expansion_ratio_milli 1,000,000 (1000:1), max_decoder_memory_bytes 512 MiB.
All WrapperImportPolicy default numbers (4 GiB source, 1M members, 64 MiB metadata, 16 GiB decoded, 1000:1 ratio, 512 MiB memory) are chosen without cited measurement or threat analysis.
research_needed: Measure distributions of compressed size, member count, expansion ratio and decoder memory across a real-world compressed-tar corpus and bomb corpus.
decision_needed: What default wrapper limits balance bomb resistance against legitimate archives?

statement: Decoded-child and aggregate limits are both checked against the same cumulative decoded length (no nested layers exist), so max_aggregate_decoded_bytes is currently redundant with max_decoded_child_bytes; the expansion ratio is computed against the whole compressed source length.

The default 1000:1 expansion limit refuses legitimate highly compressible inputs (zstd/xz/bzip2 of zero-filled or repetitive data; raw DEFLATE can reach ~1032:1) with EB_LEGACY_RESOURCE_POLICY_REFUSED.
evidence_in_source: inference from ratio arithmetic; no test with high-ratio data
research_needed: Measure ratio distribution of real tar.gz/zst/xz/bz2 (VM images, sparse data, logs) and test zero-file fixtures.
decision_needed: Should the default ratio limit be raised, made per-format, or replaced by absolute decoded budgets?

statement: decode requires the entire compressed source as an in-memory slice, checks max_source_bytes first, and accumulates the whole decoded child into one Vec; transport import is not streaming.
research_needed: Measure peak RSS for multi-GiB wrapped tars.
decision_needed: Is bounded-memory streaming legacy import required for v1?

statement: gzip decoding iterates concatenated members; each member requires magic 1F 8B and CM=8, reserved flag bits 0xE0 must be zero, and the member count is bounded by max_members.

gzip per-member observations: wrapper.flags, wrapper.mtime, wrapper.xfl, wrapper.os, wrapper.extra, wrapper.filename, wrapper.comment, wrapper.header_crc16; FHCRC is verified as the low 16 bits of CRC-32 (mismatch EB_WRAPPER_INTEGRITY_MISMATCH).
gzip FEXTRA, FNAME, FCOMMENT and FHCRC byte counts accumulate across all members and are bounded by max_metadata_bytes.

gzip DEFLATE output is limited during decoding via take(remaining+1) so limits apply before unbounded growth; DEFLATE failures map to EB_WRAPPER_STRUCTURE_INVALID. Test wrapper_limits_apply_before_unbounded_output (stream.rs:901-914).
Each gzip member trailer CRC-32 and ISIZE are verified before accepting output (EB_WRAPPER_INTEGRITY_MISMATCH); test gzip_members_are_independently_verified_and_concatenated (stream.rs:817-842).

ISIZE is compared as u32::try_from(member_len).unwrap_or(u32::MAX) instead of length mod 2^32, so valid gzip members decoding to 4 GiB or more fail as integrity mismatch, contradicting RFC 1952 and the export encoder's modulo ISIZE (export.rs:1297-1300).
evidence_in_source: inference from code; no >4 GiB test
research_needed: Regression test with a >4 GiB gzip member and tar.gz/pax-v1 export of a >4 GiB tar.
decision_needed: Fix ISIZE comparison to modulo 2^32 before v1?

statement: Any bytes after the last gzip member (e.g., zero padding from tape/record blocking) are parsed as another member header and refused as truncated or invalid magic.
research_needed: Survey prevalence of padded .tar.gz files and behavior of gzip/libarchive readers.
decision_needed: Should a future compatibility profile tolerate zero padding after gzip members?

statement: Zstandard decoding handles standard and skippable frames; skippable frames count as members, their payload length counts toward max_metadata_bytes, and only magic/length are observed (payload not retained). Test zstd_frames_and_skippable_frames_are_composed_and_checked (stream.rs:844-868).
A frame magic that is neither standard nor skippable Zstandard (including legacy pre-1.0 zstd frames) fails EB_WRAPPER_STRUCTURE_INVALID.
Zstandard frames declaring a dictionary ID are refused as Unsupported EB_WRAPPER_DICTIONARY_UNSUPPORTED; external dictionaries cannot be supplied.
A declared Zstandard frame content size is policy-checked against the remaining decoded budget before decoding and recorded as wrapper.frame_content_size.
Zstandard window_log_max is floor(log2(max_decoder_memory_bytes)) clamped to 10..31 (29 for the 512 MiB default, stream.rs:645-652); limits below 1 KiB are policy-refused.

A Zstandard frame whose window exceeds the configured window_log_max fails inside read_to_end and is reported as Corrupt EB_WRAPPER_INTEGRITY_MISMATCH, not as a resource-policy refusal; XZ memory-limit exhaustion is likewise mapped to integrity mismatch (stream.rs:449-451).
research_needed: Fixture: zstd --long=31 frame and XZ with large dictionary under a small memory policy; check reason codes.
decision_needed: Should decoder-memory refusals map to EB_LEGACY_RESOURCE_POLICY_REFUSED?

statement: Zstandard content checksums are verified only when a frame declares one; frames without a checksum are accepted with only the checksum flag observed, so 'frame checksums are enforced' holds only when present.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/compressed-stream-import-v1.md L31-32 claims frame checksums are enforced
evidence_in_source: inference from code; test only uses checksummed frames (stream.rs:916-929)
research_needed: Fixture: zstd frame without checksum with corrupted literals; determine accepted vs refused.
decision_needed: Should strict import require content checksums (or report integrity-unverified layers)?

statement: All Zstandard decode errors, structural or checksum, are mapped to Corrupt EB_WRAPPER_INTEGRITY_MISMATCH, conflating malformed frames with integrity failures. Test zstd_xz_and_bzip2_corruption_never_yields_accepted_plaintext (stream.rs:916-952).
XZ decoding derives a decoder memory limit in KiB from max_decoder_memory_bytes (minimum 1 KiB) and requires the XZ stream magic at offset 0.
Concatenated XZ streams are accepted; inter-stream zero padding must be a multiple of four and is observed as wrapper.stream_padding_bytes; any other trailing bytes fail EB_WRAPPER_STRUCTURE_INVALID.
XZ decodes in 64 KiB output steps with limits enforced after each step; decoder or check errors map to EB_WRAPPER_INTEGRITY_MISMATCH and a no-progress state to structure error.

XZ check-type and filter acceptance (check None, SHA-256, BCJ/delta filters) is delegated entirely to lzma-rust2 0.20.0; Entrybound code does not constrain them, so the documented 'unsupported filters/checks fail' is unverified.
evidence_in_source: none in code; no tests for check None or BCJ
research_needed: Fixtures for XZ with check None, CRC32, SHA-256, BCJ x86 and delta filters; record outcomes.
decision_needed: Must strict XZ import refuse check=None streams?

statement: XZ archive-level observations include wrapper.stream_count and wrapper.decoder_memory_limit, so the caller's policy value is recorded as foreign evidence.
decision_needed: Should caller policy values appear inside LOM foreign-evidence observations?

statement: bzip2 members must begin 'BZh' plus '1'-'9'; the declared working set digit x 100,000 x 6 bytes is checked against max_decoder_memory_bytes before decoding.
The 6x block-size working-set multiplier used to bound bzip2 decoder memory is uncited, and actual libbz2-rs-sys decode memory is unmeasured.
research_needed: Measure peak decoder memory per block-size level in bzip2 0.6.1/libbz2-rs-sys.

statement: bzip2 members decode independently in 64 KiB steps with limits enforced; CRC/decode failures map to EB_WRAPPER_INTEGRITY_MISMATCH, zero consumption to structure error; observations wrapper.member_compressed_bytes, wrapper.block_size_100k, wrapper.stream_count.

Every transport LOM ends with transport-layer observations layer.ordinal 0, layer.format, layer.decoded_child_digest (SHA-256), layer.member_count and layer.decoded_bytes; source_digest is SHA-256 of the exact outer bytes; no entries or conflicts.

Transport authorities use format 'compressed-stream' with structures gzip-member, zstd-frame, xz-stream, xz-stream-padding, xz-stream-sequence, bzip2-member, bzip2-stream-sequence and transport-layer.

Transport diagnostics: structure errors Nonconforming EB_WRAPPER_STRUCTURE_INVALID, integrity Corrupt EB_WRAPPER_INTEGRITY_MISMATCH, limits PolicyRefused EB_LEGACY_RESOURCE_POLICY_REFUSED (strings at diagnostics.rs:297, 316-318).
POSIX, pax and GNU tar claims remain foreign evidence until the strict resolver projects them into EAM.

TarImportPolicy defaults: archive 16 GiB, entries 1,000,000, single entry 4 GiB, total file bytes 16 GiB, name 1 MiB, extension 64 MiB, pax records 1,000,000, observations 8,000,000, per-subject 4,096, conflicts 1,000,000, resolutions 1,000,000.

Each ordinary header adds 19 observations (tar.rs:312-357) and extension headers add more, so the 8,000,000 observation cap binds near 420k plain entries (fewer with per-entry pax), making the 1,000,000 entry default unreachable.
research_needed: Import synthetic tars with 500k and 1M entries (with and without pax) under default policy.
decision_needed: Reconcile max_observations with max_entries, or count repeated/global observations differently?

statement: Default max_entry_bytes of 4 GiB refuses any tar member larger than 4 GiB (VM images, datasets) although pax size supports larger; value is uncited. Export strict re-import uses this default (export.rs:1363-1369).
research_needed: Corpus distribution of largest member size in real tars; test 5 GiB member import/export.
decision_needed: What default single-entry byte limit should strict tar import use?

statement: TarObservation keeps the LOM plus a full copy of the tar bytes; attach_transport prepends transport fields, sets tar layer.ordinal to 1, renames source_format 'tar+<transport>', replaces source_digest with the outer digest and records wrapper members and decoded-child digest.
looks_like_tar is dispatch-only: at least two 512-byte blocks, total length a 512 multiple, and either a valid first-header checksum or two leading zero blocks; full acceptance always runs observe.
Strict tar observation requires source length <= max_archive_bytes and a complete sequence of 512-byte records of at least 1,024 bytes; otherwise EB_TAR_STRUCTURE_INVALID or policy refusal.

Two all-zero blocks terminate the archive; a single zero block or any nonzero byte after the terminator is refused (EB_TAR_STRUCTURE_INVALID); extra zero blocks are accepted and observed as archive.trailing_zero_blocks.
evidence_in_source: unit test strict_tar_rejects_checksum_paths_links_conflicts_and_trailing_garbage (tar.rs:1927-1995); tools/tar-strict/observed-outcomes-v1.json shows Python tarfile and bsdtar accept both cases
research_needed: Probe GNU tar behavior (absent from differential evidence).
decision_needed: Will a versioned tar compatibility profile accept single-zero-block termination and trailing garbage?

statement: A tar with no end marker (e.g., truncated or streamed without terminator) is refused as 'end marker is missing'.
research_needed: Prevalence of unterminated tars produced by interrupted pipelines and permissive writers.

statement: Header checksum mismatch is Corrupt EB_TAR_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH; checksum_valid (tar.rs:1398-1428) accepts either unsigned or signed-byte sums with the checksum field treated as spaces.
evidence_in_source: unit test tar.rs:1939-1946; observed-outcomes bad-checksum case

statement: The parser reads ustar fields name, mode, uid, gid, size, mtime, typeflag, linkname, magic, version, uname, gname, devmajor, devminor and prefix, joining non-empty prefix + '/' + name, bounded by max_name_bytes.

Header magic/version are observed but never used to select layout, so old-GNU or star headers storing atime/ctime/offset/sparse data in bytes 345-500 are always read as a ustar prefix, risking corrupted paths or UTF-8 refusals.
evidence_in_source: inference; GNU tar was not probed (docs/tar-import-v1.md L107-109)
research_needed: Differential corpus of GNU tar --format=gnu/oldgnu (incremental -G with atime/ctime), star/xstar archives against GNU tar and libarchive.
decision_needed: Must the strict adapter dispatch on magic ('ustar\0' vs 'ustar  \0') before interpreting the prefix field?

statement: Numeric fields accept octal with leading NUL/space skipping (empty means 0) or GNU base-256 (0x80 flag, 0x40 sign) decoded to i64; other characters or overflow are structure errors.
An ordinary entry's payload extent uses local pax size, else global pax size, else header size; a non-canonical pax size is a structure error, and the extent must be <= max_entry_bytes.
Payload plus 512-byte padding must lie within the source and padding bytes must all be zero; nonzero padding fails EB_TAR_STRUCTURE_INVALID.

Each header yields 19 LOM fields with exact offsets: header.block (full 512 bytes), path.name, mode, uid, gid, size, mtime, header.checksum, typeflag, linkpath, format.magic, format.version, uname, gname, devmajor, devminor, path.prefix, payload.extent, payload.padding.

LOM evidence stores each 512-byte header twice (raw and interpreted) plus per-field copies and repeated global pax fields per entry; per-entry memory overhead at the 1,000,000-entry policy is unmeasured.
research_needed: Measure LOM heap bytes per entry and peak RSS for 100k/1M-entry tars.

statement: tar.uname and tar.gname are added to unsupported metadata (FidelityReport unavailable) for every archive with at least one header, even when all names are empty.
decision_needed: Should uname/gname loss be reported only when non-empty names were observed?

statement: Pax 'g'/'x' headers are bounded by max_extension_bytes and max_pax_records; unknown keys add 'tar.pax.<key>' to unsupported metadata; known keys are path, size, mtime, uid, gid, uname, gname, linkpath (tar.rs:1256-1261).

Pax atime, ctime, charset, comment, hdrcharset, SCHILY.xattr/acl/fflags, LIBARCHIVE.xattr and other vendor keys are not projected; tar import cannot capture xattrs, ACLs, atime/ctime or file flags, only reporting them as unavailable fidelity.
decision_needed: Should strict tar import map SCHILY/LIBARCHIVE xattr and ACL keys to native posix.xattrs/security.acls in a later adapter version?

statement: Only typeflag 'S' sparse is refused; GNU pax sparse formats (GNU.sparse.* keys, versions 0.0/0.1/1.0) are merely unknown pax keys, so such members appear to import as regular files containing raw sparse-map/condensed data under surrogate names with a success outcome.
refines_or_supersedes: contradicts docs/tar-import-v1.md L45-46 and L69-71 (sparse declarations refused)
evidence_in_source: inference: tar.rs:381-383 and 1256-1261 only record unknown keys; no 'GNU.sparse' string anywhere in crates
research_needed: Fixtures from GNU tar --sparse --format=pax (0.0, 0.1, 1.0) and bsdtar; verify imported content and outcome.
decision_needed: Must strict import refuse any GNU.sparse.* pax key until sparse projection is frozen?

statement: A pax mtime whose fractional digit count is not 0, 2, 6, 7 or 9 adds unsupported metadata 'tar.mtime-precision-<n>-digits'.
Pax mtime parsing: 1-2 fractional digits map to Centisecond, 3-6 to Microsecond, 7 to Hectonanosecond, 8-9 to Nanosecond; negative fractions normalize to floor seconds; no millisecond class exists.
Pax mtime values with more than nine fractional digits, or non-digit fractions, are refused as structure errors rather than truncated with a fidelity limitation.
research_needed: Survey pax mtime formats written by Python tarfile, libarchive, GNU tar, star, Go archive/tar.
decision_needed: Should over-precise pax times be refused or truncated with a declared loss?

statement: GNU 'L'/'K' records: value NUL-trimmed, must be UTF-8 (else EB_TAR_UNSAFE_PATH) and <= max_name_bytes; two differing long-name (or long-link) records before one entry create an unresolved Divergence conflict and strict import refuses.

For an ordinary entry, pending extension observations, current global and local pax fields and GNU claims attach to the entry observation; local pax and GNU claims are consumed, global pax persists; per-entry fields are capped by max_observations_per_subject.
An archive ending with a local pax header or GNU long-name/link record that has no following target entry is refused.

Observation is fail-fast: the first structural, safety or policy error aborts with a Diagnostic and no partial LOM; tar and stream observers never emit Invalid or Uninterpreted observations (only zip.rs uses them).
decision_needed: Do future tar compatibility/preservation profiles require Invalid/Uninterpreted observations and partial evidence for refused sources?

statement: resolve_strict refuses any Divergence or Irreconcilable conflict lacking a resolution (refuse_unresolved, tar.rs:1308-1327); resolved conflicts become ConversionResolution records bounded by max_resolutions.
A wrapped tar adds a Refinement resolution 'layer.transport-decoded-child' recording outer digest, decoded digest and member count.
max_total_file_bytes bounds the cumulative plaintext of regular-file entries; hardlink entries do not add bytes.
Duplicate reconciled logical paths are refused with EB_EAM_DUPLICATE_LOGICAL_PATH; tar append/update 'last member wins' semantics are not supported.
evidence_in_source: unit test empty_duplicate_ancestor_extension_and_special_cases_are_bounded (tar.rs:2113-2231); observed-outcomes duplicate-name (Python/bsdtar list both)
decision_needed: Should a compatibility profile support tar -r/-u last-wins semantics?

statement: Missing ancestors are synthesized as metadata-less directories, each recorded as an Omission resolution; a regular file, link or other non-directory occupying an ancestor position is refused as EB_EAM_FILE_AS_ANCESTOR.

Hardlink targets are resolved against the full reconciled path set (forward references accepted, order-independent) and must be regular files; missing targets or links to non-regular entries (including other hardlinks) are Irreconcilable refusals.
Accepting forward hardlink references differs from sequential tar readers, which require the target to precede the link, and refusing link-to-hardlink chains may reject archives some writers produce.
research_needed: Differential test of forward and chained hardlinks against GNU tar, bsdtar, Python tarfile.

statement: All hardlink group members must match the target's executable, mode, uid, gid and mtime or strict import fails with divergence; group id is hardlink_group_id(content digest, sorted deduplicated paths).

Every non-synthesized entry receives core.executable, core.mtime, posix.mode, posix.uid, posix.gid and, when grouped, posix.hardlink-group; hardlinks become File entries sharing the target ContentObject; symlinks become Symlink entries.

Tar provenance adapter_id is '<source_format>-strict/v1' (tar-strict/v1, tar+gzip-strict/v1, ...), import_mode 'strict'; divergence/irreconcilable counts come from LOM conflicts and are always zero on success because unresolved ones refuse.
Tar import always passes preservation None to planning: exact-source tar preservation (feature 0x4000 style) is not implemented.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/tar-import-v1.md L96-97 (tar preservation not defined by v1)
decision_needed: Is tar exact-source preservation needed for v1 migration/sidecar workflows?

statement: --compat and --preserve are refused for every non-ZIP source (tar, tar.*, 7z, standalone transports) with Unsupported EB_ECF_UNSUPPORTED_REQUIRED_FEATURE; the tar module exposes only observe/resolve_strict/import_strict.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/legacy-observation-model-v1.md L91-92; docs/compressed-stream-import-v1.md L71-72; docs/migration-workflows-v1.md L106-108
evidence_in_source: CLI code; tar.rs:577-858 has only strict resolver
research_needed: Runtime matrices (GNU tar, bsdtar, Python tarfile, Go) needed to define tar compatibility rules.
decision_needed: Will v1 ship any tar/7z compatibility or preservation profile?

statement: Path authority precedence is local pax path, then global pax path, then GNU long name, then ustar prefix/name; a pax path differing from a GNU long name is a divergence refusal.
A global pax 'path' is applied to every subsequent entry lacking a local path, which makes later entries collide and be refused as duplicates.

Typeflag mapping: '5' directory; NUL, '0', '7' regular file; '1' hardlink; '2' symlink; '3' character device, '4' block device, '6' FIFO, 'S' GNU sparse and any other typeflag are Unsupported EB_TAR_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.
Device nodes, FIFOs, GNU sparse, multi-volume ('M'), volume labels ('V'), GNU dumpdir ('D') and other special typeflags are refused rather than projected or reported.
decision_needed: Should special files be projected (with dangerous-restoration policy) in a later tar adapter version?

statement: V7-style directories (typeflag NUL/'0' with a trailing '/') are refused as divergence rather than treated as directories as GNU tar and libarchive do.
research_needed: Corpus/differential test of pre-POSIX tars.
decision_needed: Should a compatibility profile interpret trailing-slash regular entries as directories?

statement: A directory typeflag whose path lacks a trailing '/' is accepted with an Omission resolution 'used explicit directory typeflag'.

Directories and symlink/hardlink entries must have zero selected payload size (Irreconcilable otherwise); pax-selected size may not exceed the observed extent; POSIX 'hardlink with data' is unsupported.
Regular files and directories carrying header linkname, GNU long-link or local pax linkpath evidence are refused as divergence; a global pax linkpath is not checked here (asymmetric).
posix.mode is header mode masked to 0o7777, so setuid/setgid/sticky bits are kept and file-type bits above 0o7777 are silently discarded without a fidelity record; executable is any 0o111 bit.
decision_needed: Should discarded high mode bits be reported as a fidelity limitation?

statement: Pax or header uid/gid above u32 are refused as structure errors rather than reported as a fidelity loss, and uname/gname are never projected; ownership-name semantics remain deferred.
research_needed: Survey tar archives with uid/gid > 2^32-1 (NFSv4 idmaps, containers).
decision_needed: Should ownership names/large ids be representable in native metadata?

statement: Link target selection is local/global pax linkpath, then GNU long-link, then header linkname; pax vs GNU mismatch diverges; empty target is irreconcilable; symlink targets stay exact LinkTarget bytes (e.g., '../outside' accepted); hardlink targets must be safe UTF-8 LogicalPaths.

Pax-over-header and local-over-global differences for path, size, mtime, uid, gid (and uname/gname between pax levels) and GNU long name over header name are recorded as resolved Refinement conflicts naming the selected authority.

Pax records require a canonical decimal length (no leading zero) framing the exact record, a trailing newline, UTF-8 key and value, and a non-empty key; a repeated key in one header is Refinement if identical, unresolved Divergence (refused) if different.
Non-UTF-8 pax values (e.g., hdrcharset=BINARY) and non-UTF-8 header names (tar.rs:1378-1382) are refused; raw-byte filenames from legacy tars cannot be imported.
research_needed: Prevalence of non-UTF-8 names in real tars (legacy Latin-1/Shift-JIS).
decision_needed: Is a non-UTF-8 path encoding needed in LogicalPath for legacy import?

statement: When a later global or per-entry pax header overrides an earlier value for the same key, a resolved Refinement conflict is recorded.

Tar paths: one trailing '/' is stripped; empty, absolute, backslash-rooted, any backslash, NUL, drive-letter ':' at byte 1, and empty/'.'/'..' components are refused as EB_TAR_UNSAFE_PATH without normalization.
evidence_in_source: unit test tar.rs:1948-1965; observed-outcomes path-traversal case

statement: Because '.' components are refused and not normalized, very common tars whose members start with './' (tar -C dir -cf x.tar ., Debian data.tar) are refused by strict import.
evidence_in_source: inference from code; no test for './' prefixes
research_needed: Measure prevalence of './'-prefixed members in a release-tarball/distribution-package corpus.
decision_needed: Should strict or a compatibility profile canonicalize a leading './' component (and the '.' root entry)?

statement: Tar FidelityReport always lists captured core.executable, core.mtime, posix.mode, posix.uid, posix.gid, posix.hardlink-group, symlink-target and legacy.conversion-provenance regardless of presence; unavailable lists unsupported metadata; platform is 'legacy:tar' even for wrapped sources.
Tar authorities use format 'tar' with structures tar-layer, tar-end, tar-header, pax-global, pax-local, gnu-long-name, gnu-long-link; provenance renders authorities as 'format:structure:instance'.

Tar diagnostics: structure Nonconforming EB_TAR_STRUCTURE_INVALID; divergence EB_TAR_CONFLICT_DIVERGENCE; irreconcilable EB_TAR_CONFLICT_IRRECONCILABLE; unsafe path EB_TAR_UNSAFE_PATH; unsupported kind Unsupported EB_TAR_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE; limits PolicyRefused EB_LEGACY_RESOURCE_POLICY_REFUSED.

Tar import is fully in memory: the observation copies the whole source, each file's plaintext is copied during resolution and cloned again into planner input, so peak memory is a multiple of the decoded tar size.
research_needed: Measure peak RSS versus input size for 1, 4 and 16 GiB tars (bare and wrapped).
decision_needed: Is bounded-memory/streaming legacy import required before v1?

statement: Tar tests do not cover GNU pax sparse, './' prefixes, old-GNU/star headers, V7 directories, non-UTF-8 names, >9-digit pax times, members >4 GiB, observation-cap vs entry-cap limits, or global pax linkpath; there are no integration tests under crates/*/tests for legacy import/export.
evidence_in_source: grep of crates/*/tests found no legacy references
research_needed: Build a tar conformance corpus with observed-outcome matrix (GNU tar, bsdtar, Python, Go).

statement: No fuzz targets exist for the tar/pax observer or the gzip/zstd/xz/bzip2 transport observers (no cargo-fuzz or fuzz_target found in the repository).
research_needed: Coverage-guided fuzzing campaign for observe(), parse_pax, stream::decode.
decision_needed: Is fuzzing of legacy parsers a v1 release gate?

statement: The differential evidence records Entrybound's duplicate-name refusal reason as 'EB_DUPLICATE_LOGICAL_PATH', but the code emits 'EB_EAM_DUPLICATE_LOGICAL_PATH' (diagnostics.rs:210), so the checked evidence is stale or was not machine-generated from the current build.
evidence_in_source: string comparison of evidence file and diagnostics.rs
research_needed: Regenerate observed-outcomes with probe.py against the current build and add a CI consistency check.

statement: Differential evidence (Python tarfile 3.13.5, bsdtar 3.8.8, Windows host) covers only six cases: ordinary, duplicate-name, path-traversal, single-zero-end-block, nonzero-after-end, bad-checksum; GNU tar unavailable.
research_needed: Extend matrix to GNU tar, Go archive/tar, sparse, './', long names, pax variants, Linux/macOS hosts.

statement: Export adapters consume only a validated, verified EAM and never inspect ECF sections, source codec choices, Chunk physical order or host filesystem metadata.

Legacy targets never embed Entrybound-only evidence, encryption or signatures: receipts always state target_encrypted false and embedded_in_target false (also migration.rs:356); the receipt is external evidence only.

The omission reason states the frozen v1 profiles export safe logical bytes but omit newer AUX semantics (POSIX, ACL, Windows, macOS); their representation is deferred to future versioned profiles rather than broadening v1.
decision_needed: When and in which profile versions will POSIX/ACL/xattr/link semantics become exportable?

statement: Tar/pax observations outside the POSIX metadata-v1 subset are reported as unavailable fidelity with the reason 'unsupported by the POSIX metadata-v1 subset', deferring their native mapping to a later metadata/adapter version.
decision_needed: Which tar/pax metadata (xattrs, ACLs, atime/ctime, names, devices) enters the next native metadata version?

statement: Frozen export identifiers: exporter 'entrybound/legacy-export-v1'; receipts 'entrybound/export-receipt-v1' and '-v2'; profiles zip/portable-v1, tar/pax-v1, tar.gz/pax-v1, tar.zst/pax-v1, tar.xz/pax-v1, tar.bz2/pax-v1.
Export constants: ZIP UTF-8 flag bit 11, methods STORE 0 and DEFLATE 8, versions 2.0 and 4.5, u32/u16 ZIP64 sentinels; tar block 512 and octal maxima 0o77777777777 for size and mtime.

ExportTarget normalizes all tar variants to semantic target tar/pax-v1, exposes transport profile ids gzip-v1, zstd-v1, xz-v1, bzip2-v1, file extensions, and maps each target to its strict re-import format.
Only six export profiles exist: no 7z, cpio, standalone compressed stream, OCI layer, POSIX-faithful tar/pax-v2 or ZIP profile with Unix extra fields/symlinks.
decision_needed: Which additional export profiles (tar/pax-v2 with links and ownership, 7z, OCI) are required for v1 migration?

statement: ExportTarget::from_str accepts unversioned aliases (zip, tar, tar.gz, ...) mapped to v1 profiles, while ExportProfileId::parse requires the exact versioned id; the doc comment says a profile is never an unversioned runtime alias.
decision_needed: When a v2 profile exists, what should the unversioned alias 'tar' resolve to, and should aliases remain in receipts/automation?

statement: ExportOutcome strings are frozen as LOSSLESS, LOSSY and REFUSED.
Seven stable export issue categories: PATH_UNREPRESENTABLE, PATH_COLLISION, ENTRY_KIND_UNSUPPORTED, TIMESTAMP_RANGE_LOSS, TIMESTAMP_PRECISION_LOSS, METADATA_UNSUPPORTED, TARGET_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
ExportDisposition values preserved, degraded, omitted, refused are defined, but analysis never emits 'preserved' issues; only losses and refusals are listed.

AuxiliaryEvidenceSummary counts fidelity issues, conversion/preservation presence and reconstruction audits; ExportSourceSecurity (encrypted flag, signature counts/validity) is supplied by the caller and not verified by the export library.
research_needed: Audit CLI paths to confirm authenticated values are passed (lib.rs:5900 test).

statement: ExportReceipt carries source LAI/AUX/PCR, security, auxiliary summary, format/profile, outcome, issues, counts, target length and SHA-256, deterministic, strict re-import state; presence of wrapped_target selects receipt v2 while bare targets keep frozen v1 bytes.

accept: LOSSLESS always; LOSSY only with explicit approval, else PolicyRefused EB_LEGACY_EXPORT_LOSSY_APPROVAL_REQUIRED; REFUSED never, Unsupported EB_LEGACY_EXPORT_REFUSED with the first issue detail. Test lossy_requires_approval_and_receipt_is_canonical (export.rs:2254-2287).
Every receipt hard-codes deterministic=true; determinism is asserted only by same-process repeat tests, not across platforms, builds or dependency versions.
evidence_in_source: unit tests compare two in-process runs (export.rs:2077-2126, 2128-2187)
research_needed: Cross-OS/cross-arch golden-vector tests of target bytes.

statement: prepare_export validates the EAM, analyzes, fully encodes and compresses target bytes, computes length and SHA-256, and runs strict re-import before any output is created; REFUSED analysis produces no bytes. Test hostile_paths_are_refused_without_target_bytes (export.rs:2289-2326).
Outcome classification: any Refused issue gives REFUSED, else any Degraded or Omitted issue gives LOSSY, else LOSSLESS; issues are sorted and deduplicated.
Symlink and Windows ReparsePoint entries are REFUSED (ENTRY_KIND_UNSUPPORTED) by every v1 export profile, including tar, which natively supports symlinks.

tar/pax-v1 export cannot emit symlink or hardlink records, so any archive containing a symlink (including one imported from tar) cannot be exported to tar at all, and hardlinks export only as independent copies after lossy approval.
decision_needed: Is a tar/pax-v2 profile with link records required for v1 migration round-trips?

statement: posix.mode, uid, gid, hardlink-group, xattrs, sparse-map, security.acls, Windows descriptor/attributes/creation time/reparse original and macOS flags/birthtime are all METADATA_UNSUPPORTED Omitted, making the export LOSSY.
Since tar import always records posix.mode/uid/gid (tar.rs:740-746), a tar-to-Entrybound-to-tar or tar-to-ZIP round trip can never be LOSSLESS and always requires --allow-lossy.
research_needed: Usability study of migration workflows where every tar-derived export requires lossy approval.
decision_needed: Should construction-equivalent POSIX values (e.g., mode matching the executable projection) be exempt from LOSSY classification?

statement: Any metadata name/value combination not listed hits unreachable!, so a future MetadataName variant or registry type change would panic export at runtime rather than fail compilation or refuse.
decision_needed: Make export metadata analysis an exhaustive match so new metadata names cannot panic?

statement: Absent core.mtime is METADATA_UNSUPPORTED Degraded (LOSSY): zip/portable-v1 emits 1980-01-01T00:00:00Z and tar/pax-v1 emits 0 seconds.
For tar/pax-v1 a directory with core.executable false is Degraded because directory mode is fixed at 0755.
Analysis reconstructs and digest-verifies every file's logical content, and encoding reconstructs it again, so each file is materialized at least twice per export before strict re-import.
research_needed: Measure export CPU/memory overhead for large archives.

statement: Any path component containing a backslash or colon is PATH_UNREPRESENTABLE and REFUSED for every export profile.

ZIP-only path rules refuse trailing dot/space, control characters, < > " | ? *, stems CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/COM1-9/LPT1-9, whole-path Unicode-lowercase collisions and names over 65,535 bytes; tar/pax-v1 applies none of these checks.

ZIP portability checks omit Unicode normalization (NFC/NFD) collisions, COM0/LPT0 and superscript-digit device names, CONIN$/CONOUT$/CLOCK$, device stems with trailing spaces, and Windows path-length limits.
research_needed: Extraction matrix on Windows Explorer, 7-Zip, macOS Archive Utility, Info-ZIP, Python zipfile for these names.
decision_needed: Which additional name classes must zip/portable-v1 (or a v2) refuse?

statement: ZIP mtime analysis: non-second precision or nonzero nanoseconds is TIMESTAMP_PRECISION_LOSS Degraded; seconds outside signed 32-bit range are TIMESTAMP_RANGE_LOSS Degraded with clamping.
ZIP DOS timestamps are UTC-derived with 2-second resolution and silently clamped to 1980-01-01..2107-12-31 23:59:58 without an issue, relying on the 0x5455 extended timestamp for the exact i32 value.
Extractors that ignore Info-ZIP 0x5455 or treat DOS time as local time will restore clamped, 2-second-truncated or timezone-shifted mtimes for exports classified LOSSLESS.
research_needed: Observed-outcome matrix of mtime restoration across Windows Explorer, macOS Archive Utility, Info-ZIP, 7-Zip, Python zipfile, Java.
decision_needed: Should LOSSLESS require DOS-field exactness, or is the extended timestamp sufficient?

statement: For tar/pax-v1 a timestamp whose nanoseconds contradict its declared precision class is TIMESTAMP_PRECISION_LOSS REFUSED.
logical_content rebuilds a ContentObject from its chunk-reference order, failing Nonconforming on unknown objects/chunks and Corrupt EB_INTEGRITY_CONTENT_DIGEST_MISMATCH when the SHA-256 differs.

Export destructures ContentRef irrefutably as Internal; ContentRef has only the Internal variant (eam/model.rs:95-98), so external content references and incremental base chains do not exist in the model.
evidence_in_source: code: irrefutable let and single-variant enum
decision_needed: Are external content references/incremental archives in v1 scope?

statement: ZIP layout: local headers and data in canonical EAM entry order, then central directory, then ZIP64 EOCD/locator when needed, then classic EOCD.

ZIP entries: directories end in '/', directories and empty files STORE; other files DEFLATE level 6 only when strictly smaller than STORE; external attributes are Unix mode (0100644/0100755/040644/040755) << 16 with DOS 0x20 or 0x10.

Byte-exact frozen targets depend on pinned encoders (flate2 =1.1.9 DEFLATE level 6, zstd =0.13.3 level 9, lzma-rust2 =0.20.0 preset 6, bzip2 =0.6.1 best, Cargo.toml L16-41); any backend/version change alters frozen profile bytes and target SHA-256.
evidence_in_source: Cargo.toml exact pins; no golden-vector tests
research_needed: Golden target-byte vectors checked in CI across platforms; test effect of dependency upgrades.
decision_needed: Freeze profiles by golden vectors and vendor encoders, or define profiles semantically without byte identity?

statement: ZIP local headers set version-needed 20, or 45 with a ZIP64 extra carrying both sizes when either size reaches 0xFFFFFFFF; general flag is always UTF-8 (bit 11); no data descriptors.
ZIP central records use version-made-by (3<<8)|version-needed (Unix creator), ZIP64 extra containing only sentinel fields in specification order, empty comment, disk 0 and internal attributes 0.
ZIP64 EOCD and locator are written when entry count >= 0xFFFF or central offset/size >= 0xFFFFFFFF; the classic EOCD then carries sentinels; archive comment is empty.
Calendar conversion uses Howard Hinnant's integer civil-from-days algorithm, independent of host timezone and platform.

Wrapped tar targets compose tar/pax-v1 bytes with a transport and self-validate via stream::decode, requiring exactly one member and byte-identical tar or failing Corrupt EB_LEGACY_EXPORT_TARGET_INVALID. Test compressed_tar_profiles_are_deterministic_compositions (export.rs:2128-2187).

Export self-validation and strict re-import use default import policies, so representable exports exceeding them (ratio >1000:1, compressed output >4 GiB, member >4 GiB, gzip ISIZE wrap, ~420k+ entries) fail with an error rather than a typed REFUSED issue.
evidence_in_source: inference from export.rs:1260, 1363-1369 and stream.rs/tar.rs defaults; untested
research_needed: Stress exports: 1 GiB zero file to tar.gz/xz/zst/bz2; 5 GiB member; 1M entries.
decision_needed: Should export validation use export-specific limits derived from the source EAM?

statement: tar.gz/pax-v1 is one gzip member: raw DEFLATE level 6, header CM=8, FLG=0, MTIME=0, XFL=0, OS=255, no extra/name/comment/HCRC, trailer CRC-32 and length mod 2^32.
tar.zst/pax-v1 is one Zstandard frame at level 9 with checksum and content size present, no dictionary id, long-distance matching disabled, pledged size equal to the tar length.
tar.xz/pax-v1 uses lzma-rust2 XzOptions preset 6; single-block output and CRC64 check are asserted in a comment as library defaults, not set explicitly in code.
research_needed: Test asserting block count and check ID in generated XZ.

statement: tar.bz2/pax-v1 uses bzip2 Compression::best (block size 900k).

Strict re-import must preserve entry count, path and order, kind (directory/file), and exact file bytes; LOSSLESS additionally requires re-import LAI equal to source LAI; failures are Corrupt EB_LEGACY_EXPORT_TARGET_INVALID. Test zip_and_tar_are_deterministic_and_strictly_reimportable (export.rs:2077-2126).

For LOSSY exports only core.executable and core.mtime differences are checked against declared issues; other semantic differences are not compared, so 'differs only where typed issues predict' is enforced for two fields only.
research_needed: Property tests comparing full source vs re-imported metadata against issue lists.

statement: Strict re-import runs a complete legacy import with CompressionProfile::Fast native planning, so every export also pays a full import and replanning of the generated target.
research_needed: Measure export time/memory overhead attributable to re-import.

statement: tar/pax-v1 encodes entries in canonical EAM order and ends with exactly two zero blocks, without record-size (e.g., 10,240-byte) padding.

tar entry framing: a pax 'x' header named PaxHeaders/<16-hex ordinal> (mode 0644, mtime 0) carries mtime when not header-representable, path when not ustar-splittable, or size beyond octal; base header uses PaxFiles/<16-hex ordinal> for pax paths; mode 0755/0644; uid/gid 0; empty uname/gname.
tar headers use 'ustar\0' magic and '00' version, NUL-terminated zero-padded octal numeric fields, and a six-digit octal checksum followed by NUL and space; device fields remain zero bytes.
split_ustar_path puts paths up to 100 bytes in name, otherwise splits at the rightmost '/' yielding name <=100 and prefix <=155 bytes; no split yields a pax path.

Pax payloads list keys lexically with self-inclusive decimal lengths and refuse '=' in keys or newline in values as a policy error. Test pax_time_and_record_bytes_are_frozen_and_exact (export.rs:2584-2592).

LogicalPath permits newlines, but a newline-containing path over 100 bytes fails pax encoding with an error instead of a typed REFUSED issue, while shorter ones are written raw into the ustar name; pax length framing would allow newlines.
decision_needed: Should newline/control-character paths be classified in analysis (REFUSED or allowed) consistently for tar?

statement: pax mtime decimals use 0, 2, 6, 7 or 9 fractional digits by precision class; negative values are written as the mathematically equivalent decimal (e.g., -1.500000000). Test pax_nanoseconds_reimport_without_logical_identity_loss (export.rs:2594-2621).
Receipt v1 canonical JSON has fixed field order and trailing newline, includes target_encrypted false and embedded_in_target false, and omits strict re-import fields.
Receipt v2 adds semantic_target, transport_target, inner_tar_byte_length, inner_tar_sha256, strict_reimport_validated and reimport_lai.
Bare ZIP/tar exports are strict-reimport validated, but receipt v1 cannot express that state or the re-import LAI, so v1 receipt consumers cannot audit validation.
decision_needed: Introduce a receipt version for bare targets that records re-import validation?

statement: Canonical JSON is hand-serialized: only quote, backslash, \n, \r, \t and other U+0000-U+001F are escaped; non-ASCII and U+2028/U+2029 are emitted raw; no JSON library or RFC 8785 conformance.
research_needed: Validate receipts/reports against RFC 8785 (JCS) and independent JSON parsers.
decision_needed: Adopt a normative canonical JSON specification (e.g., JCS) for receipts and migration reports?

statement: An empty archive exports to a 22-byte ZIP and a 1,024-byte tar, both strictly re-importing to the same LAI.
Test indexed_and_stream_physical_layouts_export_identically shows INDEXED, STREAM and Dense-profile archives of the same EAM export byte-identical targets for all six profiles.
Export is entirely in memory (target Vec, per-file reconstruction, compression, re-import); there is no streaming export to a sink for archives larger than RAM.
decision_needed: Is streaming legacy export required for v1?

statement: CLI in-module tests cover tar/standalone-wrapper convert, deterministic ZIP/tar export with receipt and dry run, multi-target publish transactions, sidecar source binding, and encrypted export security transition.
Migration planning is deliberately free of filesystem transaction logic; it prepares deterministic artifacts and one canonical report, and callers commit publication.
Migration report format is 'entrybound/migration-report-v1' with version 1.
MigrationOutcome values READY, LOSSY_APPROVAL_REQUIRED, REFUSED, PUBLISHED and FAILED.
MigrationOutcome::Failed is never constructed anywhere in the workspace, so no FAILED migration report is ever produced despite the documented state.
decision_needed: Should failed transactions emit a FAILED report, or should FAILED be removed from v1?

statement: Per-target report records target, outcome, issues, lossy approval, output path, produced flag, artifact length and SHA-256, strict re-import state and LAI, and relation_to_native ('same-source-eam').

SidecarMigrationReport records source format and SHA-256, import mode, compatibility profile, conflict/resolution counts, exact-source preservation, sidecar path/length/SHA-256 and verification result; sidecar LAI/AUX/PCR are carried in the parent source_* fields (CLI lib.rs:1858-1862).
MigrationReportV1 canonical JSON uses fixed field order, target records sorted by profile id, compact encoding, trailing newline, and the key 'overall_publish_outcome'.

prepare_migration validates the EAM once, collapses duplicate targets, orders by profile id, runs full export preparation per target; REFUSED dominates LOSSY_APPROVAL_REQUIRED, and any non-READY outcome clears all artifacts (all-or-nothing).
Any prepare_export error for one target (for example a resource-policy failure during self-validation) aborts the whole migration with a Diagnostic instead of a per-target REFUSED record.
decision_needed: Should per-target validation failures be reported inside the migration report?

statement: lossy_approved is true whenever the outcome is not LOSSY or lossy output is allowed, so LOSSLESS and REFUSED targets are reported as lossy_approved true.
decision_needed: Should lossy_approved be null or false for non-LOSSY targets?

statement: PreparedMigration holds every accepted target's full bytes simultaneously in memory, so peak memory is the sum of all requested legacy artifacts.
research_needed: Measure memory for multi-target publish of large archives.

statement: mark_published sets PUBLISHED and produced=true for all targets without setting output paths; paths are filled by the caller.
Every migration target record hard-codes target_encrypted false and entrybound_signatures_embedded false.

prepare_sidecar encodes the imported EAM as INDEXED or STREAM, reopens it with the matching reader, and requires provenance source_digest equal to SHA-256 of the exact legacy bytes (else Corrupt EB_INTEGRITY_AUX_MISMATCH) and identical LAI/AUX/PCR (else EB_INTEGRITY_LAI_MISMATCH); the source is never mutated.
Sidecars always use default WriteOptions/StreamWriteOptions and bootstrap sequential limits; the API offers no encryption, signing or planner options for sidecars.
decision_needed: Should sidecars support encryption/signing at creation time?

statement: Migration JSON string escaping duplicates the export module's hand-written escaper (same rules), so the two canonical JSON writers must be kept in sync manually.
